function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "The red block remains on the table and cannot be delivered to the bowl within the remaining budget. All four closing attempts caught air: the tilted wrist camera made its image center a misleading aim reference, so repeated +x corrections each undershot, and the final attempt revealed a +y offset instead. With one decision left I can at most reposition or close, not regrasp, ferry the block ~12cm to the bowl, and release it inside.", "hindsight": "1) The wrist camera is tilted: its image center is not the fingertip point (closed tips project ~90px below center), and a block centered in the wrist image is actually tens of mm further +x than the jaws - wrist-view py mostly encodes depth, not x. Grasp aiming must use the fixed side/front cameras or verify with the measured gripper value after closing (~0.016 = air, intermediate = holding). 2) move_to per call advances only ~15-25% of the commanded gap at ~6-9mm per step, with step count roughly gap/40mm; gripper open/close commands take ~80 steps (4s) each. 3) Table at z=0.80, the ~45mm block top sits at z~0.845; commanding eef z~0.86 puts the pads at block mid-height. 4) The blue bowl is near x=+0.05..0.11, y=0..0.05 with the opening up; approach it from a high hover, not at low altitude. 5) A y-offset as small as ~20mm makes the jaws close beside the block - verify both lateral axes at pad depth before closing."}
